claim_summary: For each integer \(N\ge2\), hopping \(J>0\), and one-terminal capture rate \(\kappa>0\), let \(H_N\) be the uniform nearest-neighbor path Hamiltonian with diagonal terminal loss \(-i\kappa/2\), and set \(g=\kappa/(2J)\). When \(N\) is odd, exactly one simple eigenvalue of \(H_N\) lies on the negative imaginary axis for every \(g>0\). When \(N\) is even, define \(g_N=\min_{u>0}\cosh((N+1)u)/\sinh(Nu)\). The minimum is unique; there are zero, one, or two distinct negative-imaginary eigenvalues according as \(g<g_N\), \(g=g_N\), or \(g>g_N\), with a genuine second-order exceptional point at equality. These even-length thresholds strictly decrease, satisfy \(g_N>1\), and obey \(g_N=1+[\log(4N)+1+o(1)]/(2N)\) as even \(N\to\infty\). No claim is made about exceptional points outside the imaginary axis.
integrity: All-dimensional proof by recurrence, strict convexity, tridiagonal eigenspace uniqueness, and exponential minimizer asymptotics; numerical checks are supplementary.
scientific_limitations: Spectral classification concerns only the strictly negative imaginary axis for a uniform path with one terminal Markovian absorber; no global classification of off-axis degeneracies.
The result does not characterize optimal mean capture time or Liouvillian exceptional points.
Publication-priority assessment is conditional on inspected evidence; some full texts are unavailable.
title: Parity-selected overdamped poles and a logarithmic exceptional-point shift in terminally lossy quantum paths
